title: Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
summary: Anomaly detection methods struggle with data exhibiting varying local densities, where distance-based methods miss local anomalies and density-based methods require careful parameter selection and incur quadratic time complexity. SVEAD constructs an ensemble of random Voronoi diagrams by sampling anchors, scores points by normalized cell-relative distance weighted by local scale, and averages scores across partitions. Across 45 ADBench datasets it achieves the highest average AUC-ROC (0.8538) and AUC-PR (0.5000) among 12 baselines, including 0.9339 AUC-ROC on cardio, while maintaining linear time and constant space complexity.

approach: Route is paper_only with no author repository on disk (only an uncloned anonymous.4open.science link), so SVEAD is reimplemented from the paper: for each of t=100 partitions, sample m anchors uniformly without replacement, assign every point to its nearest anchor in standardized feature space (implicit Voronoi, no cell boundaries), score each point as (delta/delta_max) * delta_mean inside its cell, skip singleton cells, and average the per-partition scores. The match target is C1: AUC-ROC 0.9339 on ADBench cardio (1831 samples, 21 features, 176 anomalies); the dataset is fetched at runtime through a validated fallback chain (ADBench GitHub raw -> OpenML cardiotocography -> UCI Cardiotocography), all of which reduce to exactly the same 1831x21 table with 176 positives, and a hard validation gate asserts that shape before any scoring. The m hyperparameter is grid-searched over {2,4,...,256} with 5 seeded repeats per value and t=100, matching the paper's protocol (R7, R8); we report both the label-tuned best m and the full m-curve so the +/-0.0189 tolerance band is interpretable, plus AUC-PR (C2) for free from the same runs. C3/C4 (45 datasets) and C5/C6 (GPU 500k-instance scalability) are explicitly out of scope on this CPU-only machine and are flagged as 'not reproduced' in the output.
steps: Install/verify deps: `pip install numpy scipy pandas scikit-learn matplotlib requests tqdm openpyxl xlrd`; confirm sklearn.datasets.fetch_openml and sklearn.metrics imports succeed.

Write svead/data.py with a priority loader and an on-disk cache at data/cardio.npz: (1) local cache; (2) ADBench GitHub — GET https://api.github.com/repos/Minqi824/ADBench/git/trees/main?recursive=1, find any path containing 'cardio' ending in .csv/.npz/.arff, download via raw.githubusercontent.com; (3) sklearn.datasets.fetch_openml(data_id=1466) or name='cardiotocography' — take the 21 feature columns, keep rows with NSP in {1,3}, label = (NSP == 3); (4) UCI fallback https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/193/cardiotocography.zip -> CTG.xls, same 21-feature/NSP filter.

Validate the loaded table in svead/data.py: assert X.shape == (1831, 21), y.sum() == 176, mean(y) ~= 0.0961, no NaN/inf (assumption A6); if any assertion fails on a fallback source, log the mismatch into the provenance dict and continue, because the source is then not guaranteed to be the ADBench cardio table.

Write svead/svead_core.py: sample_anchors(X, m, rng) -> unique row indices (R1); assign_cells(X, A, chunk_rows) -> (cell_ids, delta) using chunked Euclidean distance and argmin with lowest-index tie-break (R2, R11); cell_stats -> per-cell delta_max and delta_mean computed for all points before any scoring (R4); score_partition -> s = (delta / delta_max) * delta_mean with NaN for singleton cells and a delta_max == 0 guard (R3, R5); svead_score(X, m, t, seed) -> nanmean over t partitions, 0 if all NaN, plus diagnostics (cell-size histogram, skipped fraction, per-partition seconds) (R6, R12).

Write svead/metrics.py: roc_auc_score wrapper, average_precision_score (primary AUC-PR), trapezoidal precision_recall_curve AUC (secondary), and summarize(list) -> mean/std/min/max; all functions take scores first and labels second so labels are consumed only post-prediction (R9, R10).

Run the smoke test: `python experiments/smoke_test.py`. Part A: synthetic 300x6 with 10% Gaussian outliers, m=4, t=3 -> assert finite non-negative scores, shape (300,), AUC-ROC > 0.8. Part B: real cardio, m=8, t=5 -> assert score shape (1831,), deterministic repeat for the same seed, total runtime < 60 s.

Run the pre-full-run intermediate checks below (dataset signature, standardization stats, anchor uniqueness, cell-size/skip diagnostics, a kNN-distance and IsolationForest sanity baseline, single-run timing extrapolation).

Write experiments/run_cardio.py: outer loop over m in the 8-value grid, inner loop over the 5 seeds, each run calling svead_score on the standardized matrix with t=100, recording AUC-ROC, AUC-PR (both variants), wall time, skipped-point fraction and cell statistics; append rows to results/per_m_table.csv and dump raw per-run records to results/raw_cardio.json.

Launch the full suite: `python experiments/run_cardio.py`; after the first two m values finish, check that the extrapolated total stays inside the budget (expected total is only a few minutes because the per-run cost is ~0.1-3 s at these sizes) and only then let it complete.

Select best m = argmax of mean AUC-ROC across the 5 seeds; compute mean/std for AUC-ROC and AUC-PR at that m, and also record the fixed-m=128 (A3 fallback) result and the full m-curve for sensitivity.

Write reproduce.py: load data from cache, reuse or regenerate results/raw_cardio.json, run selection, then write results/metrics.json with (a) C1 value vs 0.9339 with the 0.0189 band and PASS/FAIL verdict, (b) C2 value vs 0.5356, (c) per-m table and per-repeat spreads, (d) dataset provenance and validation flags, (e) timing, (f) the assumption ledger entries applied, (g) an explicit not_reproduced block for C3, C4, C5 and C6 (45-dataset average and GPU/500k scalability are out of scope on CPU).

Run the final entrypoint `python reproduce.py` and read results/metrics.json; report the reproduced C1 with its spread, label the overall verdict partially_reproduced, and never present C3-C6 as reproduced.
smoke_test: `python experiments/smoke_test.py` — synthesizes 300x6 data with 10% outliers at m=4, t=3 and asserts finite non-negative scores, shape (300,), AUC-ROC > 0.8; then scores the full 1831x21 cardio table at m=8, t=5, asserting shape (1831,), reproducible scores for a repeated seed, and under 60 s wall clock. This exercises download -> standardize -> anchor sampling -> nearest-anchor assignment -> cell stats -> scoring -> averaging -> AUC end to end on a few seconds of compute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset signature: X.shape == (1831, 21), y.sum() == 176, anomaly rate 0.0961, zero NaN/inf, and the 21 UCI/ADBench feature names present — abort or flag loudly if a fallback source yields different counts (e.g. 2126 rows means the suspect class was not filtered).
Standardization: after StandardScaler, per-column mean ~ 0 (|mean| < 1e-9) and std ~ 1 for all 21 columns; confirm the scaler is fit with no label access.
Anchor sampling: for every m in the grid and every seed, sampled anchor indices are distinct and len == m (requirement R1), verified on 20 random (m, seed) pairs.

Cell diagnostics: for m=256 on n=1831, singleton cells must be essentially zero and skipped-point fraction < 0.5%; log non-empty cell count, max/mean cell size, and skipped fraction for every (m, seed).

Score sanity: all scores finite and >= 0; distribution roughly right-skewed with a handful of large scores matching injected/synthetic outliers; Spearman correlation with a trivial 1-NN mean-distance baseline is clearly positive.

Sanity baselines on cardio: sklearn IsolationForest(n_estimators=100, random_state=1) and a global kNN mean-distance score; both should land roughly in 0.65-0.85 AUC-ROC — if SVEAD cannot beat them, the reimplementation is wrong, not the paper.
No-cell-means-0 check: with the chosen cell_stats_scope (anchor included at distance 0), delta_mean must still be > 0 for every non-singleton cell; assert this before the full run.

Timing probe: time one full run at m=256, t=100 -> extrapolate the whole 40-run grid; if the extrapolation exceeds ~25 minutes, drop to 3 repeats and/or m in {8,16,32,64,128} (documented as a reduced protocol).
Determinism: two back-to-back runs with identical (m, seed) produce bitwise-identical score vectors.
budget_plan: Total ~90 min on CPU. Setup and data acquisition 15 min (pip installs, the ADBench/OpenML/UCI fallback chain, cache write, dataset-signature validation). Implementation of svead/data.py, svead/svead_core.py and svead/metrics.py 20 min. Smoke test and intermediate checks 10 min (including the IsolationForest/kNN sanity baselines and the timing probe). Full cardio grid 25 min reserved though expected ~5-10 min (8 m values x 5 seeds x t=100 on a 1831x21 matrix; each run is only a few seconds, so sum over m of m makes the whole grid roughly 2x the cost of a single m=256 run per seed). Final reproduce.py + metrics.json writing and interpretation 10 min. Contingency: if a run ever exceeds the projection, first cut repeats from 5 to 3, then narrow the m grid to four values, always recording the reduced protocol in results/metrics.json. C3/C4 (45 datasets) and C5/C6 (500k-instance CPU/GPU timing) are deliberately not scheduled.

"""SVEAD: Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection.

Reimplementation from the paper description (arXiv:2601.03664, "Stochastic
Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection", Cao et al.).

Pipeline per partition k = 1..t:
  1. sample m anchors uniformly from X without replacement          (R1)
  2. assign every point to its nearest anchor (Euclidean)           (R2, R11)
  3. per cell: delta_max = max ||x - a||, delta_mean = mean ||x-a||  (R4)
  4. score s(x) = (delta / delta_max) * delta_mean                  (R3)
     singleton cells (|C| == 1) are skipped in that partition       (R5)
  5. final score = arithmetic mean over the t partitions            (R6)

Labels are never touched here: this module only produces scores.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

import numpy as np

__all__ = [
    "sample_anchors",
    "assign_cells",
    "cell_stats",
    "score_partition",
    "svead_score",
    "PartitionDiagnostics",
]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# R1: anchor sampling
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def sample_anchors(n: int, m: int, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
    """Sample ``m`` distinct row indices uniformly without replacement (R1)."""
    m = int(min(m, n))
    return rng.choice(n, size=m, replace=False)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# R2 / R11: implicit Voronoi assignment (nearest-anchor query only)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def assign_cells(
    X: np.ndarray,
    anchors: np.ndarray,
    chunk_rows: int = 2048,
) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Assign each row of ``X`` to its nearest anchor.

    Returns ``(cell_ids, delta)`` where ``cell_ids[i]`` is the index (into
    ``anchors``) of the nearest anchor to row ``i`` and ``delta[i]`` is the
    Euclidean distance to it.  No cell boundaries or vertices are ever built
    (R11); membership comes purely from nearest-anchor queries (R2).

    Ties are broken towards the lowest anchor index (assumption A5).
    """
    X = np.ascontiguousarray(X, dtype=np.float64)
    A = np.ascontiguousarray(anchors, dtype=np.float64)
    n = X.shape[0]
    m = A.shape[0]
    cell_ids = np.empty(n, dtype=np.int64)
    delta = np.empty(n, dtype=np.float64)

    # squared anchor norms, reused for every chunk
    a_sq = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", A, A)

    for start in range(0, n, chunk_rows):
        stop = min(start + chunk_rows, n)
        block = X[start:stop]                       # (b, d)
        # squared Euclidean distances via the expansion ||x-a||^2 = |x|^2+|a|^2-2 x.a
        d2 = (
            np.einsum("ij,ij->i", block, block)[:, None]
            + a_sq[None, :]
            - 2.0 * (block @ A.T)
        )
        np.maximum(d2, 0.0, out=d2)
        cell_ids[start:stop] = np.argmin(d2, axis=1)   # lowest index on ties
        delta[start:stop] = np.sqrt(d2[np.arange(stop - start), cell_ids[start:stop]])
    return cell_ids, delta


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# R4: per-cell statistics, computed before any scoring
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def cell_stats(
    cell_ids: np.ndarray, delta: np.ndarray, m: int
) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Return ``(delta_max, delta_mean, counts)`` per cell (R4).

    ``delta_max[j]``  = max distance of the points assigned to cell j
    ``delta_mean[j]`` = mean distance of the points assigned to cell j
    ``counts[j]``     = |C_j| (the anchor itself is a member of its own cell,
                        at distance 0, exactly as in Eq. (2) of the paper).
    """
    counts = np.bincount(cell_ids, minlength=m).astype(np.float64)
    sums = np.bincount(cell_ids, weights=delta, minlength=m)
    maxima = np.full(m, -np.inf, dtype=np.float64)
    # np.maximum.at is slow; use a sort-free reduction via np.maximum.reduceat
    order = np.argsort(cell_ids, kind="stable")
    sorted_ids = cell_ids[order]
    sorted_delta = delta[order]
    boundaries = np.searchsorted(sorted_ids, np.arange(m + 1))
    for j in range(m):
        lo, hi = boundaries[j], boundaries[j + 1]
        if hi > lo:
            maxima[j] = sorted_delta[lo:hi].max()
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
        delta_mean = np.where(counts > 0, sums / np.maximum(counts, 1.0), 0.0)
    delta_max = np.where(counts > 0, np.maximum(maxima, 0.0), 0.0)
    return delta_max, delta_mean, counts


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# R3 / R5: within-cell scoring
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def score_partition(
    cell_ids: np.ndarray,
    delta: np.ndarray,
    delta_max: np.ndarray,
    delta_mean: np.ndarray,
    counts: np.ndarray,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Score every point inside its cell: s = (delta/delta_max) * delta_mean.

    Points whose cell holds only the anchor (|C| == 1) get ``NaN`` so that the
    ensemble average can skip them (R5).  A degenerate cell with
    ``delta_max == 0`` (all members coincide with the anchor) also yields NaN.
    """
    dmax = delta_max[cell_ids]
    dmean = delta_mean[cell_ids]
    cnt = counts[cell_ids]
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        rel = np.where(dmax > 0, delta / np.where(dmax > 0, dmax, 1.0), np.nan)
    s = rel * dmean
    s = np.where(cnt > 1, s, np.nan)
    return s

"""Dataset resolution for the ADBench ``cardio`` table.

Priority order (first hit wins, everything is cached under REPRO_DATA_CACHE):
  1. local cache ``<cache>/6_cardio.npz`` (the official ADBench Classical artifact)
  2. ADBench GitHub raw file ``adbench/datasets/Classical/6_cardio.npz``
  3. OpenML ``cardiotocography`` (data_id 1466) filtered to NSP in {1,3}
  4. UCI CTG archive -> CTG.xls, same 21-feature / NSP filter

The loaded table is validated against the signature reported in Table 3 of the
paper (1831 samples, 21 features, 176 anomalies, 9.61% anomaly rate).  Labels
are returned separately and are never used by the scoring code (R10).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import urllib.request
import zipfile
from typing import Dict, Tuple

import numpy as np

CACHE = os.environ.get(
    "REPRO_DATA_CACHE", os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".cache", "datasets", "files")
)

EXPECTED = {"n": 1831, "d": 21, "n_anomalies": 176, "anomaly_rate": 0.0961}

ADBENCH_RAW = (
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Minqi824/ADBench/main/"
    "adbench/datasets/Classical/6_cardio.npz"
)
OPENML_ID = 1466
UCI_URL = "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/193/cardiotocography.zip"

CACHE_FILES = ["6_cardio.npz", "cardio_adbench.npz", "cardio.npz"]


def _validate(X: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, source: str) -> Dict[str, object]:
    n, d = X.shape
    n_anom = int(y.sum())
    rate = float(y.mean())
    ok = (
        n == EXPECTED["n"]
        and d == EXPECTED["d"]
        and n_anom == EXPECTED["n_anomalies"]
        and abs(rate - EXPECTED["anomaly_rate"]) < 5e-4
        and np.isfinite(X).all()
    )
    return {
        "source": source,
        "n": int(n),
        "d": int(d),
        "n_anomalies": n_anom,
        "anomaly_rate": round(rate, 6),
        "nan_or_inf": int((~np.isfinite(X)).sum()),
        "matches_paper_table3": bool(ok),
    }


def _from_npz(path: str, source: str) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, Dict[str, object]]:
    z = np.load(path, allow_pickle=False)
    X = np.asarray(z["X"], dtype=np.float64)
    y = np.asarray(z["y"]).astype(int).ravel()
    if y.min() < 0:  # ADBench sometimes stores {-1, 1}
        y = (y > 0).astype(int)
    return X, y, _validate(X, y, source)


def _download(url: str, dest: str) -> str:
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(dest), exist_ok=True)
    if os.path.exists(dest) and os.path.getsize(dest) > 0:
        return dest
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 repro"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as r, open(dest, "wb") as f:
        f.write(r.read())
    return dest


def _from_openml() -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, Dict[str, object]]:
    from sklearn.datasets import fetch_openml

    bunch = fetch_openml(data_id=OPENML_ID, as_frame=True, cache=True)
    df = bunch.frame.dropna()
    feat = [c for c in df.columns if c not in ("NSP", "CLASS", "Target")]
    X = df[feat].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    y = (df["NSP"].astype(float).to_numpy() == 3.0).astype(int)
    return X, y, _validate(X, y, f"openml:{OPENML_ID}")


def _from_uci() -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, Dict[str, object]]:
    import pandas as pd

    zp = _download(UCI_URL, os.path.join(CACHE, "cardiotocography_uci.zip"))
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zp) as zf:
        xls = [n for n in zf.namelist() if n.lower().endswith(".xls")]
        with zf.open(xls[0]) as fh:
            df = pd.read_excel(fh, sheet_name="Data", header=0)

def run(X, m, t=100, seeds=range(1, 6), exclude_anchor=False, divide_by_t=False):
    rocs, prs = [], []
    for seed in seeds:
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        n = X.shape[0]
        tot = np.zeros(n); cnt = np.zeros(n)
        for _ in range(t):
            idx = sample_anchors(n, m, rng)
            A = X[idx]
            cid, delta = assign_cells(X, A)
            dmax, dmean, counts = cell_stats(cid, delta, m)
            if exclude_anchor:
                # recompute mean over non-anchor members only
                sums = np.bincount(cid, weights=delta, minlength=m)
                anchor_cid = cid[idx]
                sums[anchor_cid] -= 0.0  # anchor distance is 0 anyway
                cnts = counts.copy()
                cnts[anchor_cid] -= 1
                dmean = np.where(cnts > 0, sums / np.maximum(cnts, 1), 0.0)
                dmax = dmax.copy()
                # max unchanged (anchor dist 0 never the max unless singleton)
            with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
                rel = np.where(dmax[cid] > 0, delta / np.where(dmax[cid] > 0, dmax[cid], 1.0), np.nan)
            s = rel * dmean[cid]
            s = np.where(counts[cid] > 1, s, np.nan)
            ok = ~np.isnan(s)
            tot[ok] += s[ok]; cnt += ok
        denom = np.full(n, float(t)) if divide_by_t else cnt
        sc = np.where(denom > 0, tot / np.where(denom > 0, denom, 1.0), 0.0)
        rocs.append(auc_roc(sc, y)); prs.append(auc_pr(sc, y))

"""Variant probe 2: raw UCI features, with-replacement anchors, other scalings."""
import os, sys, zipfile
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from svead import load_cardio, auc_roc, auc_pr
from svead.svead_core import assign_cells, cell_stats

CACHE = os.environ["REPRO_DATA_CACHE"]
X, y, prov = load_cardio(verbose=False)


def run(X, m, t=100, seeds=range(1, 6), replace=False):
    rocs, prs = [], []
    n = X.shape[0]
    for seed in seeds:
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        tot = np.zeros(n); cnt = np.zeros(n)
        for _ in range(t):
            idx = rng.choice(n, size=m, replace=replace)
            A = X[idx]
            cid, delta = assign_cells(X, A)
            dmax, dmean, counts = cell_stats(cid, delta, m)
            with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
                rel = np.where(dmax[cid] > 0, delta / np.where(dmax[cid] > 0, dmax[cid], 1.0), np.nan)
            s = rel * dmean[cid]
            s = np.where(counts[cid] > 1, s, np.nan)
            ok = ~np.isnan(s)
            tot[ok] += s[ok]; cnt += ok
        sc = np.where(cnt > 0, tot / np.where(cnt > 0, cnt, 1.0), 0.0)
        rocs.append(auc_roc(sc, y)); prs.append(auc_pr(sc, y))
    return np.mean(rocs), np.std(rocs, ddof=1), np.mean(prs), np.std(prs, ddof=1)


with zipfile.ZipFile(os.path.join(CACHE, "cardiotocography_uci.zip")) as zf:
    xls = [n for n in zf.namelist() if n.lower().endswith(".xls")]
    with zf.open(xls[0]) as fh:
        df = pd.read_excel(fh, sheet_name="Data", header=0)
df = df.dropna()
feat = [c for c in df.columns if c not in ("NSP", "CLASS", "Target")]
Xr = df[feat].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
yr = (df["NSP"].astype(float).to_numpy() == 3.0).astype(int)
print("raw UCI:", Xr.shape, int(yr.sum()), "same labels as adbench:", np.array_equal(yr, y))

from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler, MinMaxScaler, RobustScaler

variants = {
    "raw": Xr,
    "std(ddof0)": StandardScaler().fit_transform(Xr),
    "minmax": MinMaxScaler().fit_transform(Xr),
    "robust": RobustScaler().fit_transform(Xr),
}
for name, M in variants.items():
    for m in [2, 3, 4, 8]:
        r = run(M, m)
        print(f"{name:11s} m={m:3d}  ROC {r[0]:.4f}+/-{r[1]:.4f}  PR {r[2]:.4f}+/-{r[3]:.4f}")

print("\n-- with-replacement anchors on ADBench artifact --")
for m in [2, 3, 4, 8]:
    r = run(X, m, replace=True)
    print(f"replace m={m:3d}  ROC {r[0]:.4f}+/-{r[1]:.4f}  PR {r[2]:.4f}+/-{r[3]:.4f}")

"""Dataset resolution for the ADBench ``cardio`` table.

The data path is frozen to the official ADBench Classical artifact
``6_cardio.npz`` (cached under REPRO_DATA_CACHE).  It already validates exactly
against Table 3 of the paper: 1831 samples, 21 features, 176 anomalies,
9.61% anomaly rate, no NaN/inf.

Every other source (ADBench GitHub raw, OpenML 1466, UCI CTG zip) is a
best-effort fallback wrapped in try/except: on any failure it logs the
provenance and returns ``None`` instead of raising.  Rows are never mixed
between sources -- ``X`` and ``y`` always come from a single provenance key.

Labels are returned separately and are never used by the scoring code (R10).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import urllib.request
import zipfile
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

import numpy as np

CACHE = os.environ.get(
    "REPRO_DATA_CACHE",
    os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".cache", "datasets", "files"),
)

EXPECTED = {"n": 1831, "d": 21, "n_anomalies": 176, "anomaly_rate": 0.0961}

#: frozen primary artifact (ADBench Classical dataset #6)
PRIMARY_CACHE_FILES = ["6_cardio.npz", "cardio_adbench.npz", "cardio.npz"]

ADBENCH_RAW = (
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Minqi824/ADBench/main/"
    "adbench/datasets/Classical/6_cardio.npz"
)
OPENML_ID = 1466
UCI_URL = "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/193/cardiotocography.zip"


def _validate(X: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, source: str) -> Dict[str, object]:
    n, d = X.shape
    n_anom = int(y.sum())
    rate = float(y.mean())
    ok = (
        n == EXPECTED["n"]
        and d == EXPECTED["d"]
        and n_anom == EXPECTED["n_anomalies"]
        and abs(rate - EXPECTED["anomaly_rate"]) < 5e-4
        and bool(np.isfinite(X).all())
    )
    return {
        "source": source,
        "n": int(n),
        "d": int(d),
        "n_anomalies": n_anom,
        "anomaly_rate": round(rate, 6),
        "nan_or_inf": int((~np.isfinite(X)).sum()),
        "matches_paper_table3": bool(ok),
    }


def _from_npz(path: str, source: str) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, Dict[str, object]]:
    z = np.load(path, allow_pickle=False)
    X = np.asarray(z["X"], dtype=np.float64)
    y = np.asarray(z["y"]).astype(int).ravel()
    if y.size and y.min() < 0:  # ADBench sometimes stores {-1, 1}

def _download(url: str, dest: str) -> str:
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(dest), exist_ok=True)
    if os.path.exists(dest) and os.path.getsize(dest) > 0:
        return dest
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 repro"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as r, open(dest, "wb") as f:
        f.write(r.read())
    return dest


def _from_openml() -> Optional[Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, Dict[str, object]]]:
    from sklearn.datasets import fetch_openml

    bunch = fetch_openml(data_id=OPENML_ID, as_frame=True, cache=True)
    df = bunch.frame.dropna()
    feat = [c for c in df.columns if c not in ("NSP", "CLASS", "Target")]
    X = df[feat].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    y = (df["NSP"].astype(float).to_numpy() == 3.0).astype(int)
    return X, y, _validate(X, y, f"openml:{OPENML_ID}")


def _from_uci() -> Optional[Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, Dict[str, object]]]:
    import pandas as pd

    zp = _download(UCI_URL, os.path.join(CACHE, "cardiotocography_uci.zip"))
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zp) as zf:
        xls = [n for n in zf.namelist() if n.lower().endswith(".xls")]
        with zf.open(xls[0]) as fh:
            raw = pd.read_excel(fh, sheet_name="Data", header=None)
    raw = raw.iloc[2:].reset_index(drop=True)  # CTG.xls carries two header rows
    df = raw.dropna(subset=list(range(10, 31)) + [45])
    X = df.iloc[:, 10:31].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    y = (df[45].astype(float).to_numpy() == 3.0).astype(int)
    return X, y, _validate(X, y, "uci:193")


def load_cardio(
    verbose: bool = True,
) -> Tuple[Optional[np.ndarray], Optional[np.ndarray], Dict[str, object]]:
    """Return ``(X, y, provenance)`` for the ADBench cardio dataset.

    ``X``/``y`` are ``None`` if no source could be resolved; ``provenance``

            attempts.append(f"cache:{name}")

"""Full cardio protocol: SVEAD m-grid x 5 seeds at t=100 (paper Sec. 5.1).

For every m in {2^1, ..., 2^8} and every seed in {1..5} the SVEAD ensemble is
run with t = 100 partitions on the ADBench cardio table.  AUC-ROC and AUC-PR
are computed from the scores only after scoring is finished (R9, R10).

Outputs (both under results/):
  results/per_m_table.csv   one row per (m, seed)
  results/raw_cardio.json   the same records plus diagnostics, machine readable
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import json
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from svead import auc_pr, auc_pr_trapz, auc_roc, load_cardio, svead_score

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(HERE)
RESULTS = os.path.join(ROOT, "results")

M_GRID = [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256]  # {2^1, ..., 2^8}  (R7)
SEEDS = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]                   # 5 repeats           (R8)
T = 100                                   # ensemble size       (R7)

FIELDS = [
    "m",
    "seed",
    "t",
    "auc_roc",
    "auc_pr",
    "auc_pr_trapz",
    "seconds",
    "skipped_fraction",
    "n_nonempty_cells",
    "n_singleton_cells",
    "max_cell_size",
    "mean_cell_size",
    "all_skipped_points",
]


def main() -> int:
    os.makedirs(RESULTS, exist_ok=True)

    X, y, prov = load_cardio()
    if X is None:
        print("[run_cardio] no dataset resolved; aborting")
        return 1
    print(f"[run_cardio] cardio X={X.shape} anomalies={int(y.sum())} ({prov})")

    rows = []
    t_start = time.perf_counter()
    for m in M_GRID:
        for seed in SEEDS:
            scores, diag = svead_score(
                X, m=m, t=T, seed=seed, return_diagnostics=True
            )
            rec = {
                "m": m,
                "seed": seed,
                "t": T,
                "auc_roc": auc_roc(scores, y),
                "auc_pr": auc_pr(scores, y),
                "auc_pr_trapz": auc_pr_trapz(scores, y),
                **diag.as_dict(),
            }
            rows.append(rec)
            print(
                f"  m={m:4d} seed={seed}  AUC-ROC {rec['auc_roc']:.4f}"
                f"  AUC-PR {rec['auc_pr']:.4f}"
                f"  skip={rec['skipped_fraction']:.4f}"
                f"  {rec['seconds']:.2f}s"
            )
        agg = [r for r in rows if r["m"] == m]
        print(
            f"m={m:4d} MEAN  AUC-ROC {np.mean([r['auc_roc'] for r in agg]):.4f}"
            f" +/- {np.std([r['auc_roc'] for r in agg], ddof=1):.4f}"
            f"   AUC-PR {np.mean([r['auc_pr'] for r in agg]):.4f}"
            f" +/- {np.std([r['auc_pr'] for r in agg], ddof=1):.4f}"
        )

    total = time.perf_counter() - t_start

    csv_path = os.path.join(RESULTS, "per_m_table.csv")
    with open(csv_path, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=FIELDS)
        w.writeheader()
        for r in rows:
            w.writerow({k: r.get(k) for k in FIELDS})

    json_path = os.path.join(RESULTS, "raw_cardio.json")
    with open(json_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(
            {
                "dataset": "cardio",
                "provenance": prov,
                "m_grid": M_GRID,
                "seeds": SEEDS,
                "t": T,
                "total_seconds": total,
                "records": rows,
            },
            fh,
            indent=2,
        )
    print(f"[run_cardio] wrote {csv_path} and {json_path} in {total:.1f}s")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

import time

    y = np.zeros(n, dtype=int)

The clean re-run exits 0 in 15.3 s and reproduces C1 at AUC-ROC 0.9300 +/- 0.0024 versus the paper's 0.9339, a 0.0039 gap well inside the 0.0189 tolerance; C2 also passes at 0.5240 versus 0.5356. The full m grid {2^1..2^8}, t=100, and five seeds were run on the full 1831-sample ADBench cardio table, so no scale-down is present and no reported result is hard-coded or copied from the paper. The main caveats are that m was selected by maximizing AUC-ROC on the same labels (the paper does not state the grid-search criterion, A10) and the code's default ensemble denominator is the number of scored partitions rather than t, though at selected m=2 there are no singleton cells and the two are identical. requirement_check.evidence: svead/svead_core.py sample_anchors uses rng.choice(n, size=m, replace=False); diagnostics show anchors_unique=true at the selected m.
assign_cells computes chunked squared Euclidean distances and argmin over anchors; no cell boundaries or vertices are constructed.
cell_stats computes per-cell counts, sums, and maxima before score_partition; delta_max and delta_mean are passed into scoring.
score_partition sets NaN for cells with count <= 1 and svead_score accumulates only non-NaN scores; no singleton cells occur at m=2, but the skip rule is implemented.

The default ensemble aggregation divides by the number of partitions that scored the point, not literally by t; the divide_by_t variant is reported and is identical at selected m=2 because no singleton cells occur. The target value is unaffected, but the default is not the literal divide-by-t rule.
M_GRID=[2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256] and T=100 are used; the full 8-value grid is run and m=2 is selected by mean AUC-ROC.
SEEDS=[1,2,3,4,5] are run and metrics report mean/std over the five repeats.
metrics.py uses roc_auc_score and average_precision_score (plus a trapezoidal PR-AUC variant); both C1 and C2 are reported.

The scoring modules never receive labels; labels are used only in metrics.py. However reproduce.py selects m by maximizing mean AUC-ROC over the same labels, so labels influence hyperparameter selection; the paper does not state the grid-search criterion (A10).
assign_cells determines membership solely through nearest-anchor queries; no explicit Voronoi cell boundaries are built.
Each partition does chunked O(n*m*d) nearest-anchor assignment and t=100 partitions are looped, giving O(n*m*d*t); memory is bounded by the chunk_rows x m distance block.
